claims.text: The catalyst initially has a predominantly reduced, oxide-free surface after preparation under inert conditions.
Increasing the applied electrochemical potential promotes formation of a surface oxide layer.
A dynamic, ultrathin platinum oxide or oxide/hydroxide overlayer forms on the nanoparticle surfaces near the oxide-formation potential.
The density and stability of the oxide overlayer govern catalytic behavior.
The oxide or hydroxide overlayer provides active oxygen species.
Active oxygen species from the overlayer aid adsorption and oxidation of ethanol intermediates.
The overlayer facilitates removal of adsorbed poisoning intermediates.
The overlayer enables coordinated or synchronized electron and proton transfer steps.
Formation of the overlayer increases ethanol-oxidation activity.
Formation of the overlayer improves ethanol-oxidation product selectivity.
Formation of the overlayer improves catalyst durability.
An oxide-promoting potential regime will produce higher current density than an oxide-suppressing regime.
An oxide-promoting potential regime will yield improved product selectivity relative to the reduced-surface baseline.
An oxide-promoting potential regime will cause slower performance degradation than the reduced-surface baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies under electrochemical conditions permitting oxide formation and may fail outside the oxide-formation potential regime or in non-electrochemical environments.
